brief: Identify repair or maintenance costs that a purchase price does not cover.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Maintenance Planning"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Planea más allá de comprar"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Planeje além da compra"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Identify repair or maintenance costs that a purchase price does not cover.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: Homes and vehicles keep needing care after purchase; plan fictional dollars for scheduled work and uncertain repairs.
instruction.misconception: A purchase budget covers maintenance forever or a scheduled service is an unforeseeable emergency.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: Save toward known maintenance dates; keep uncertain repairs separate. An estimate helps planning but does not guarantee the final bill.
A known service date supports advance planning.
Existing reserved money reduces the remaining amount to save.
Funding the purchase does not fund later care.
Excluded damage makes the final cost uncertain.
A known recurring inspection can be budgeted in advance.
Known maintenance and uncertain faults need distinct planning.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
